clue.text: Society tries wrong random number generators

indicators.note: random arrangement means the letters of these two words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A society's attempts at making random-number generators keep going wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number generators' looks like computing, but a number here is a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A number is a piece of music, so the people who produce them are composers of popular tunes.

clue.text: Lily's better half's home, getting frisky

indicators.note: frisky means lively and playful, so these letters jump about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Lily's partner, once home, starts feeling amorous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lily' looks like a woman's name; it is a plant. Christmas imagery fits the flower's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant, Ornithogalum, is a bulb of the lily family with white star-shaped flowers.

clue.text: Natural water flowing north

indicators.note: in a down clue, flowing north means the word runs upwards, read backwards

parts.note: Evian is a French brand of bottled mineral water

explanation.surface: Natural water is flowing northwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unaffected and artless, untouched by worldliness, is simple and innocent.

clue.text: Liable to see red snake burrowing into pine

indicators.note: something burrowing into another goes inside it

parts.note: to pine for something is to wish for it
the asp is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: A snake burrows into a pine tree and is apt to see red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pine' is a verb, to long for, not the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Being irritable and quick to anger, with a sharp sting, is like being prone to lose one's temper.

clue.text: How explorers are engaged with legal procedure

definitions.meaning: explorers are out searching, ... of something, read as two words
a judicial inquiry, as held by a coroner into a death

explanation.surface: Explorers get caught up in a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A coroner's investigation into a sudden death is a formal judicial hearing, and explorers are out searching.

clue.text: Inscription I used between record and chart

indicators.note: between places the I in the middle, with the record before and the chart after

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
a graph is a chart of data

explanation.surface: An inscription was used between a record and a chart.
explanation.definitionFit: An engraved motto on a building or statue, or a quotation heading a book, is a short engraving or legend.

clue.text: Jolt from spirits, Irish lagers and wine

parts.note: shorts are small measures of spirits
Harp is an Irish lager brand
hock is a German white wine

explanation.surface: A shock from mixing spirits, Irish lagers and wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer was a British prison policy of brief harsh punishment; Harp is a lager brewed in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief, severe punishment meant to deter is a sudden blow to the system, a sharp jolt.

clue.text: Bold wife cutting girdle fastening

indicators.note: cutting means the piece slices into the middle of the other

parts.note: a sash is a band worn round the waist, like a girdle
buckling is fastening with a buckle

explanation.surface: A wife cuts through the clasp of a girdle, a bold act.
explanation.definitionFit: Daring and swaggering, like a pirate hero of adventure films, is dashing and daring.

clue.text: The Guardian's going to fill top post, offering good facilities

parts.note: the paper speaking says we'll, short for we will, meaning we're going to
to fill a post is to appoint someone
the ED, the editor, holds the top post at a newspaper

explanation.surface: The Guardian announces it will fill its top job, with good perks.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's newspaper speaks as 'we', so its 'going to' is WE'LL.
explanation.definitionFit: A house or hotel that is properly equipped and furnished is described as having fine amenities.

clue.text: Empty white sign for flags

indicators.note: an emptied word loses its insides, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: Aries, the ram, is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A white sign with nothing on it is used in place of flags.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to grow tired, and something that wears someone out tires them, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Don unknown old pretty clothes

indicators.note: to clothe something is to wrap around it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: pretty, as in pretty good, means quite
X is the algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A university don, of no known name, dresses in old pretty clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like a university fellow or the verb to put on; it is the Spanish title of Cervantes's knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Cervantes's hero is styled Don, the Spanish honorific, so the title alone points to the knight.

clue.text: Relish one shot, a boundary

indicators.note: shot in the sense of ruined or wrecked tells us these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A cricketer savours one shot that went for a boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boundary' suggests a cricket hit, but it is where land meets the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The edge of the sea or a lake marks the limit of the land, a natural border.

clue.text: Animal got nourishment, taken in hands

indicators.note: something taken in is held inside, so one piece sits between the other's letters

parts.note: R and L are right and left, the two hands
to have eaten is to have got nourishment

explanation.surface: An animal is fed by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The honey badger of Africa and Asia is a carnivorous mammal, a fair example of a beast.

clue.text: Nanny rating Times covers

indicators.note: covers means the outer piece goes round the inner one

parts.note: by means times, as in three by four
a rating is an ordinary sailor, an AB or able seaman

explanation.surface: A nanny rates the Times newspaper's covers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nanny' is a verb here, meaning to pamper.
explanation.definitionFit: To nanny someone is to fuss over and mollycoddle them, which is what treating someone like an infant means.

clue.text: Stop talking twice before work's close

indicators.note: before places the stop-talking pieces ahead of the work

parts.note: shut up is a blunt order to stop talking
twice says the order to stop talking is given a second time, in its short form sh
op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: Someone is told twice to be quiet before the workday ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' looks like part of 'work's close', the end of the day, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To shut up shop is an idiom for stopping trading for the day or for good, ceasing business.

clue.text: Foolish Sally lifted up jumper

parts.note: a sally is a witty remark, a crack

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a jumper is a top, a garment worn on the upper body

explanation.surface: Sally raised her jumper, a foolish act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a name; it is a quip.
explanation.definitionFit: A crazy, eccentric scheme or person is regarded as daft or barmy.

clue.text: Suffering from cold, maybe curator has shivers

indicators.note: shivers suggests the letters are shaken about into a new order

explanation.surface: A museum curator with a chill is shivering.
explanation.definitionFit: Catarrh is the mucus of a head cold, so the adjective describes someone suffering from a streaming nose.

clue.text: I see rising value in bookmaking family's home

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: ah is an exclamation meaning I see
worth means value

explanation.surface: Value is seen rising in a bookmakers' family business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bookmaking' suggests betting, but the family wrote books: the Brontës lived at this Yorkshire village's parsonage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brontë sisters, novelists, lived at the parsonage in this West Yorkshire village.

clue.text: Star with lowered head? A cape's in need of a trim

indicators.note: the first letter is moved down to the bottom of the word

parts.note: the sun is a star
Cape Horn is the southern tip of South America

explanation.surface: A star with a bowed head wonders if a cape needs trimming.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair or fleece that has not been cut has grown long and wants cutting.

clue.text: Bar Council pens instruction for one on the fiddle

definitions.text: instruction for one on the fiddle

indicators.note: pens means encloses, so the letters sit inside these two words

explanation.surface: The barristers' governing body writes rules for a lawyer guilty of fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the fiddle' suggests fraud; here it is a violinist.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the Italian marking tells string players to resume playing with the bow after pizzicato.

clue.text: One wearing ring turned a pale colour

indicators.note: turned means the whole assembly is read backwards
one wearing another is inside it, as a body inside clothes

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone wearing a ring has gone pale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts I inside CALL to give CALIL, which 'turned' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: The shrub's flowers give their name to a soft pale purple shade.

clue.text: Briefly want right-wingers ruling state

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to want something is to wish for it
cons is short for Conservatives, the right-wing party
a party that is ruling is in, in power

explanation.surface: Right-wing politicians want, in short, to rule the state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' drops the last letter of WISH.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the fifty constituent members of the USA, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Beat off a gathering of people

parts.note: a light that is off is out
a do is a party, a social gathering

explanation.surface: People at a gathering beat it off.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass or outperform a rival is to defeat them.

clue.text: Mobile phone ring right for loser

indicators.note: mobile means moving about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone whose mobile phone has a ring set to suit a loser.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with no chance of success, a hopeless case, is a born failure.

clue.text: Result where French book's taken around

parts.note: ou is French for where

indicators.note: the book takes in, or holds, the other piece

parts.note: a tome is a large book
C, for circa, means around a date

explanation.surface: A French book was taken around somewhere, with some result.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome is the consequence or effect of events, what they lead to in the end.

clue.text: Politician with dull look Chinese prepare to fire

parts.note: a matt finish is a dull, non-glossy look
the Han are the main ethnic group of China
to cock a gun is to make it ready to fire

explanation.surface: A dour-looking politician gets ready to sack a Chinese colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a British Conservative politician, health secretary during the Covid pandemic.
explanation.definitionFit: He was a Conservative MP and cabinet minister, so the bare word politician defines him.
